items.policy_summary: NCD 140.9, effective 2016-08-30, leaves medical-necessity decisions to MACs case by case; it establishes neither blanket national coverage nor national exclusion.
items.policy_scope: National delegation to local review; checked 2026-09-16.
items.comparison: Same surgical techniques for different diagnoses may face different prerequisites.
items.disparity_evidence: Historical Medicare survey: surgery covered without in-network provider ARR 1.84 versus private insurance. Medicare claims show geographic variation in surgery receipt; neither study establishes current claim approval rates or causality.
items.evidence_type: National policy; Medicare claims and survey; observational clinical evidence
items.limitations: Coverage eligibility is not an approval guarantee; surgeon availability and local criteria matter.
items.next_question: Compare requests, denials, appeals and prerequisites across MACs for equivalent indications.

items.medicare_part: D; some provider-administered drugs may be B
items.policy_summary: Potential outpatient drug coverage depends on the specific drug, medically accepted indication, formulary and utilization rules. A national promise to cover every hormone product or formulation was not established.
items.policy_scope: Part D benefit framework; individual 2026 formularies require verification.
items.comparison: Compare the same hormone by diagnosis, formulation and payer.
items.disparity_evidence: Clinical review found mental-health and quality-of-life associations. A historical insurance survey examined hormone denials, but its Medicare estimate has inconsistent confidence-interval and p-value signals.
items.evidence_type: General benefit policy; systematic clinical review
items.limitations: Off-label indication support and drug-specific restrictions need individual verification.
items.next_question: Which products and indications face authorization, step therapy, tiering or exclusions?

items.item: Anatomy-appropriate services when recorded sex conflicts
items.indication: Otherwise covered sex-specific screening or treatment
items.policy_summary: Claims Manual chapter 32, section 240, effective 2010-04-01, provides condition code 45 for institutional claims and KX for applicable professional procedure lines to bypass sex-related edits.
items.policy_scope: National claims processing; ordinary coverage rules still apply.
items.comparison: Otherwise comparable claims with and without a sex/procedure mismatch.
items.disparity_evidence: CMS recognizes erroneous rejection risk. Medicare research warns modifiers alone cannot reliably identify transgender beneficiaries.
items.evidence_type: Documented administrative mechanism; Medicare measurement study
items.limitations: No present-day denial rate established; KX has unrelated uses.
items.next_question: Measure initial rejection, corrected payment, appeal burden and delay.

items.item: Bone mass measurement: estrogen-deficient risk category
items.policy_summary: Estrogen deficiency plus clinical osteoporosis risk is an explicit eligibility pathway. Generally covered every 24 months, or more often if medically necessary; assignment eliminates cost sharing.
items.comparison: Men of comparable fracture risk lack this particular eligibility pathway.
items.disparity_evidence: Historical Medicare data found substantially more DXA testing among women than men; this does not isolate coverage as the cause.
items.evidence_type: Explicit sex-specific criterion; Medicare utilization study
items.limitations: Different underlying risk and screening recommendations complicate direct comparison.
items.next_question: Compare beneficiaries at equivalent fracture risk and identify their qualifying indications.

items.item: Bone mass measurement: men and other qualifying groups
items.indication: Specified imaging abnormalities, steroids, hyperparathyroidism or treatment monitoring
items.population: Men and women meeting qualifying criteria
items.policy_summary: Men can qualify through sex-neutral categories, including specified imaging findings, steroid therapy, primary hyperparathyroidism and osteoporosis-treatment monitoring. Age alone is not among the listed eligibility categories.
items.comparison: Sex-specific estrogen pathway versus remaining eligibility categories.
items.disparity_evidence: A randomized MAPD outreach program increased post-fracture male testing, showing that delivery barriers can persist despite coverage.
items.evidence_type: National policy; Medicare Advantage randomized intervention
items.limitations: Low utilization does not prove denied claims; outreach trial involved one insurer and selected men.
items.next_question: Separate referral failures, benefit eligibility, denials and patient access barriers.

items.population: Eligible beneficiaries; anatomy and treatment history matter
items.policy_summary: Medicare lists one baseline mammogram for women aged 35–39 and annual screening from age 40. Medically necessary diagnostic mammograms follow separate rules.
items.policy_scope: National benefit; current Medicare page checked 2026-09-16.
items.comparison: Transgender versus cisgender patients with comparable breast anatomy and risk.
items.disparity_evidence: A 2024 review found heterogeneous screening differences, including studies with no difference.
items.limitations: Clinical screening eligibility differs after surgery and hormone exposure; evidence is not Medicare-specific.
items.next_question: Compare eligible anatomy-defined groups and track marker-related claim errors.

items.item: PSA and digital rectal prostate screening
items.population: Medicare eligibility language specifies men over 50; retained prostate requires consideration
items.policy_summary: Annual screening after age 50; screening PSA has no cost sharing, while digital rectal examination generally has deductible and coinsurance. NCD 210.1 current version effective 2006-06-19.
items.comparison: Transgender women with retained prostate versus cisgender men.
items.disparity_evidence: BRFSS study found lower screening odds, attenuated after adjustment for clinician recommendations and discussions.
items.evidence_type: National coverage; non-Medicare observational screening study
items.limitations: Screening frequency is not necessarily appropriate-care quality; hormone exposure alters clinical context.
items.next_question: Distinguish clinician recommendation, informed preference and claim denial.

items.item: IUD insertion solely for pregnancy prevention
items.indication: Pregnancy prevention without separate medical indication
items.population: Reproductive-age beneficiaries, frequently eligible through disability
items.medicare_part: B; MA supplemental coverage requires verification
items.policy_summary: WPS article A55951 states insertion code 58300 is noncovered and offers an alternative billing pathway for endometrial disease. This row documents WPS nonpayment for contraception; nationwide method-specific coverage was not independently established.
items.policy_scope: WPS Part B article, revised 2026-06-25; local-source exclusion. Do not generalize to all MACs, Part D drugs or MA supplemental benefits.
items.comparison: Pregnancy prevention versus treatment of the same organ's disease.
items.disparity_evidence: Medicare studies found lower contraceptive utilization than Medicaid and increased use after gaining dual coverage.
items.evidence_type: MAC coding policy; Medicare claims and quasi-experimental evidence
items.limitations: Methods and payer components differ; supplemental benefits and dual Medicaid coverage matter.
items.next_question: Verify method-specific payment, indication and benefit component in each plan.

items.population: Eligible beneficiaries, including people retaining a cervix
items.policy_summary: Pap/pelvic screening generally every 24 months, annually for specified higher-risk groups. HPV cotesting every five years at ages 30–65 without symptoms. Covered screening has no cost sharing with assignment.
items.comparison: Transmasculine versus cisgender patients with a cervix.
items.disparity_evidence: Single-center study found lower adjusted odds of up-to-date Pap testing in transgender men.
items.evidence_type: National coverage; non-Medicare observational utilization evidence
items.limitations: Study was not nationally representative or a Medicare denial audit; diagnostic follow-up differs from screening.
items.next_question: Assess anatomy-appropriate eligibility, tolerability, provider access and claim edits.

items.indication: Endometrial hyperplasia with documented medical necessity
items.population: Patients with endometrial disease meeting local criteria
items.policy_summary: WPS A55951 permits qualifying treatment using an unlisted procedure pathway instead of routinely denied IUD-insertion coding. Documentation and diagnosis requirements apply; 2026 coding changes take effect 2026-07-01.
items.policy_scope: WPS contractor guidance, not a national IUD approval.
items.comparison: Same device for treatment versus pregnancy prevention.
items.disparity_evidence: Shows indication-dependent access; national research found higher contraceptive use when noncontraceptive clinical indications were present.
items.limitations: Article concerns specific endometrial conditions; it does not establish approval for every gynecologic use.
items.next_question: Do clinically eligible patients encounter coding-related denials or regional variation?

items.item: Medically necessary infertility evaluation and treatment
items.indication: Infertility associated with a medical condition
items.policy_summary: Benefit Policy Manual chapter 15, section 20.1B, covers reasonable and necessary infertility treatment for a person ordinarily expected to be fertile. This general principle does not approve every assisted reproductive technique.
items.policy_scope: National manual; chapter 1 cites coverage since 1980-01-15.
items.comparison: Male- and female-factor infertility with comparable treatment objectives.
items.disparity_evidence: A blanket statement that Medicare excludes all infertility care conflicts with the manual.
items.evidence_type: National benefit policy; no matched disparity study attached
items.limitations: Specific technique, indication, setting and benefit category must be established.
items.next_question: Which infertility services satisfy current medical-necessity and coding rules?

items.indication: Infertility or prevention of treatment-related infertility
items.population: Patients considering gamete or embryo preservation and assisted reproduction
items.policy_summary: The national infertility manual does not itemize IVF, gamete retrieval or storage. This search did not establish a procedure-specific national approval or exclusion; each component requires MAC/plan verification.
items.policy_scope: Evidence gap in this review; not a finding of national noncoverage.
items.comparison: Sperm versus oocyte preservation, including cancer and gender-affirming treatment contexts.
items.disparity_evidence: No verified Medicare-specific comparative approval evidence retrieved.
items.evidence_type: Coverage not established at procedure level
items.limitations: General infertility coverage cannot be extrapolated to elective preservation or indefinite storage. Drugs used to promote fertility are excluded from basic Part D; see G15.
items.next_question: Obtain written component-level determinations and distinguish infertility treatment from preservation.

items.population: Beneficiaries seeking vasectomy or tubal sterilization
items.policy_summary: NCD 230.3 excludes elective procedures solely for sterilization. Surgery causing sterility can be covered when necessary to treat illness or injury. This applies to male and female procedures.
items.policy_scope: Longstanding national policy; effective date not posted.
items.comparison: Vasectomy versus tubal sterilization; prevention versus treatment indication.
items.disparity_evidence: Explicit shared exclusion; it does not mean the burdens or alternative options are equivalent.
items.limitations: Do not infer that necessary cancer surgery or all hysterectomies are excluded.
items.next_question: Compare out-of-pocket burden, available alternatives and MA/Medicaid supplemental coverage.

items.item: Prescription contraceptive pills, patches and rings
items.indication: Pregnancy prevention or noncontraceptive medical treatment
items.policy_summary: Do not extend Part B device exclusions to all Part D contraceptive drugs. Product, indication, formulary placement, utilization rules and cost sharing require plan-level review; universal no-cost coverage was not established.
items.policy_scope: Part D framework; no exhaustive 2026 formulary inventory completed.
items.comparison: Same product for prevention versus menstrual or other medical indications.
items.disparity_evidence: Gaining dual coverage was associated with higher contraceptive use, especially short-acting methods.
items.evidence_type: Plan-specific benefit framework; Medicare quasi-experimental access evidence
items.limitations: Claims capture reimbursed dispensing and may miss cash purchases or unfilled prescriptions.
items.next_question: Audit current product-level formularies, indications, rejections and patient costs.

items.policy_summary: Drugs used to promote fertility are excluded from basic Part D. Supplemental drug benefits may cover excluded drugs. A different medically accepted indication requires separate assessment.
items.policy_scope: National Part D exclusion; chapter 6 sections 20.1 and 20.3
items.comparison: Drug benefit exclusion versus potentially covered medically necessary infertility services
items.disparity_evidence: The exclusion is indication-based. This review did not establish comparative male/female claim or patient-cost effects.
items.evidence_type: Explicit national drug exclusion; disparity evidence gap
items.limitations: Do not extrapolate this drug exclusion to every infertility procedure or treatment of an underlying condition.
items.next_question: Compare patient costs and supplemental benefits by therapy, underlying condition and sex.

studies.citation: Proctor K et al. Identifying the Transgender Population in the Medicare Program. Transgender Health. 2016;1:250–265.
studies.design: Administrative claims identification and validation study
studies.data_period: 2013 claims; historical records used for validation
studies.finding: Approximately 90% had confirmatory evidence. Claims-based ascertainment yields a lower bound; sex-conflict modifiers alone were inadequate identifiers.
studies.limitation: Misses people without identifying diagnoses or reimbursed care; not a current approval-rate study.
studies.relevance: Population definitions and claims-edit audit design.

studies.citation: Almazan AN, Keuroghlian AS. Association Between Gender-Affirming Surgeries and Mental Health Outcomes. JAMA Surgery. 2021;156:611–618.
studies.population: US transgender adults seeking or having received surgery
studies.finding: Receipt of desired surgery was associated with lower psychological distress and suicidal ideation compared with wanting surgery but not receiving it.
studies.limitation: Self-report, selection and residual confounding prevent causal interpretation; does not measure Medicare coverage.
studies.relevance: Clinical context for access; not evidence of reimbursement discrimination.

studies.citation: Baker KE et al. Hormone Therapy, Mental Health, and Quality of Life Among Transgender People: A Systematic Review. J Endocr Soc. 2021;5:bvab011.
studies.population: Transgender participants across ages and settings
studies.finding: Hormone therapy was associated with better quality of life and reduced depression/anxiety; no conclusion about suicide mortality was possible.
studies.limitation: High risk of bias, small samples and co-interventions limit certainty.
studies.relevance: Clinical evidence must be distinguished from formulary access.

studies.citation: Curtis JR et al. Longitudinal Trends in Use of Bone Mass Measurement Among Older Americans, 1999–2005. J Bone Miner Res. 2008;23:1061–1067.
studies.finding: Across pooled years, 30.0% of women and 4.4% of men in analyzed white/Black populations received central DXA at least once.
studies.limitation: Historical utilization differences do not isolate policy effects, need or appropriate clinical eligibility.
studies.relevance: Documents a Medicare sex gap in bone testing without proving discrimination.

studies.citation: Pasquale MK et al. Evaluation of an Osteoporosis Outreach Program for Men With a Fragility Fracture and Their Physicians. Med Care. 2021;59:148–154.
studies.population: 10,934 men initially assigned; 7,842 analyzed at 12 months
studies.finding: BMD testing was 10.7% with outreach versus 4.9% without; osteoporosis treatment initiation was 4.0% versus 2.5%.
studies.limitation: Single insurer, post-randomization exclusions and selected untreated fracture patients; no direct sex comparison.
studies.relevance: Shows delivery interventions can improve covered care for men.

studies.citation: Chokshi M et al. Disparities in Study Inclusion and Breast Cancer Screening Rates Among Transgender People: A Systematic Review. J Am Coll Radiol. 2024;21:1430–1443.
studies.population: Transgender/gender-diverse adults receiving hormones or with top surgery
studies.finding: Several studies found lower screening, while three found no group difference; evidence and participant inclusion were limited.
studies.limitation: Heterogeneous eligibility, small samples and observational designs; no uniform pooled Medicare effect.
studies.relevance: Supports nuanced, anatomy-based screening audit rather than a universal gap claim.

studies.citation: Kalavacherla S et al. Prostate Cancer Screening Uptake in Transgender Women. JAMA Netw Open. 2024;7:e2356088.
studies.population: 255 transgender women and 1,020 cisgender men in matched cohort
studies.finding: Screening at ages 55–69 was 22.2% versus 36.3%. Differences became statistically nonsignificant after adjusting for clinician recommendations.
studies.limitation: Self-reported screening; hormone/anatomy details and causal pathways incompletely measured.
studies.relevance: Provider recommendation and clinical context may explain utilization gaps independently of benefit exclusion.

studies.citation: Peitzmeier SM et al. Pap Test Use Is Lower Among Female-to-Male Patients Than Non-Transgender Women. Am J Prev Med. 2014;47:808–812.
studies.design: Retrospective chart review with multilevel adjustment
studies.population: 350 transgender men and 4,882 women with cervices, ages 21–64
studies.finding: Transgender men had lower odds of current Pap screening: adjusted OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47–0.85.
studies.limitation: Single center, observational and mostly below standard Medicare age; not a coverage-denial study.
studies.relevance: Anatomy-appropriate access disparities may persist when screening is potentially reimbursable.

studies.citation: Bellerose M et al. Coverage Gaps and Contraceptive Use Among Medicare Enrollees With Disabilities. JAMA Netw Open. 2025;8:e2517718.
studies.design: National claims comparison plus staggered-entry difference-in-differences
studies.payer: Traditional Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and dual enrollment
studies.finding: Gaining dual coverage was associated with a 3.9-percentage-point increase in contraceptive use (95% CI 3.5–4.3); short-acting methods accounted for the largest increase.
studies.limitation: Observational transitions, claims-based measures and unmeasured cash purchases; not evidence of a male–female matched treatment effect.
studies.relevance: Direct Medicare evidence connecting benefit gaps to reproductive-health access.

studies.citation: Ellison J et al. Contraceptive Use Among Traditional Medicare And Medicare Advantage Enrollees. Health Aff. 2024;43:98–107.
studies.design: Comparative Medicare and Optum claims analysis
studies.finding: Use was higher in MA. Relative to traditional Medicare, long-acting method probability exceeded threefold and tubal sterilization tenfold; noncontraceptive indications were associated with greater use.
studies.limitation: Claims/payer selection; methods and clinical indications differ; current policy cannot be inferred from historical utilization.
studies.relevance: Separate Medicare benefit components and pregnancy prevention from medical treatment.
studies.extraction_level: Abstract plus author-institution summary for period

studies.citation: Bakko M, Kattari SK. Transgender-Related Insurance Denials as Barriers to Transgender Healthcare: Differences in Experience by Insurance Type. J Gen Intern Med. 2020;35:1693–1700.
studies.design: Weighted cross-sectional survey; adjusted risk ratios from multivariable models
studies.population: 11,320 insured transgender/nonbinary adults attempting relevant care; Medicare subgroup 283 before endpoint-specific restriction
studies.payer: Medicare, Medicaid, private, military and multiple insurance categories
studies.data_period: 2015 US Transgender Survey; experiences in preceding year
studies.finding: Medicare versus private coverage: covered surgery but no in-network provider ARR 1.84 (95% CI 1.29–2.62). This endpoint measures reported access barriers, not adjudicated claims.
studies.limitation: Nonprobability self-report; small Medicare subgroup; no traditional/MA separation. Hormone-denial estimate has CI crossing 1 despite p=.03; do not label definitive. Historical policy context.
studies.relevance: Direct Medicare subgroup evidence distinguishes nominal surgery coverage from practical provider access.
studies.extraction_level: Indexed full-text methods/results; direct PMC page blocked

studies.citation: Balkan E et al. Gender-Affirming Surgery for Transgender and Gender Diverse Medicare Beneficiaries. JAMA Netw Open. 2025;8:e258072.
studies.design: National retrospective claims study with matched comparison cohort and adjusted repeated-observation models
studies.population: 35,737 identified transgender/gender-diverse adults; 101,361 matched beneficiaries not identified as transgender
studies.payer: Traditional Medicare; excluded beneficiaries with at least six months of MA enrollment per year
studies.finding: Annual surgery receipt decreased from 2.1%–2.2% in 2016–2017 to 1.4% in 2018–2019. Regions 4 and 6 had lower adjusted odds than region 1; comparable geographic differences were absent in the comparison cohort.
studies.limitation: Claims algorithm; no surgery-demand denominator, prior surgery, cash-paid care or denied requests. MA largely excluded. Procedure inventory excluded services based on one MAC guidance; low receipt does not establish unmet need.
studies.relevance: Direct Medicare utilization evidence, with geographic differences warranting access investigation; does not establish causal discrimination or current coverage.
studies.extraction_level: Indexed full-text methods/results; direct PMC page blocked
